ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of rhombus ABCD is 6, with diagonals AC and BD intersecting at point O, and $ \angle ABC = 120^\circ$. Point P is a moving point on AC, and point E is the midpoint of AB. What is the minimum value of $PB + PE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct the line segment DE, intersecting AC at point P, and draw BP as shown in the figure: \\
Then $PB+PE=DE$, at this point $PB+PE$ has its minimum value;\\
Since in the rhombus ABCD, $\angle ABC=120^\circ$,\\
Hence, AD=BD, $\angle DAB=60^\circ$,\\
Thus, $\triangle ABD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
Since point E is the midpoint of AB,\\
Hence, DE $\perp$ AB,\\
Since $AB=BD=6$, $BE=\frac{1}{2}AB=3$, \\
Hence, $DE=\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=\boxed{3\sqrt{3}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a rhombus, with A on the left, C on the right, D above, and B below; diagonal AC is drawn as a horizontal line, diagonal BD is drawn as a vertical line, and the two intersect at O. Point E is marked on side AB, point P is marked on diagonal AC, and line segments related to P are drawn. The problem statement gives that the side length of the rhombus is 6, ∠ABC=120°, E is the midpoint of AB, and P moves on AC. Reasoning: In a rhombus, the two diagonals are perpendicular to each other and bisect each other, so AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD; therefore reflecting B with respect to AC gives the point D. Since P is on AC, the distances from P to the symmetric points B and D are equal, that is, PB=PD. Thus for any P∈AC, there is PB+PE=PD+PE. By the triangle inequality, PD+PE≥DE; equality is attained when P is taken as the intersection point of the line DE and AC, and D, P, E are collinear, so the minimum value of PB+PE is DE. Next calculate DE. Because ABCD is a rhombus, AB=AD=6; also ∠ABC=120°, and adjacent angles are supplementary, so ∠DAB=60°. In △ABD, AB=AD=6 and the included angle is 60°, so △ABD is an equilateral triangle with side length 6, hence BD=6. E is the midpoint of AB, so BE=3, and in the equilateral triangle, the line segment DE from vertex D to the midpoint E of AB is an altitude, DE⊥AB. Thus DE=√(BD²−BE²)=√(6²−3²)=√27=3√3. Therefore the minimum value is 3√3.
